change_note: One field added to each tier: price_usd_6month, the TOTAL charged for the six-month prepay term, or null when the plan is not sold on it (enterprise). Nothing was removed, renamed, or re-typed; every 2026-08-27 key survives with identical semantics, so a consumer written against the prior snapshot keeps working unchanged — which is what makes the deploy order of this wave's two repos free rather than lockstep. WHY IT WAS ADDED: the ladder published here carried only the monthly price, so the two 6-month figures were hand-typed in the algovault-bot's copy in three places (cta.py x2, messages.py x1), each of them a restated number that goes stale with nothing able to notice — the exact _TIER_QUOTA generator defect scripts/check-quota-refusal-seam.py L4 exists to make unwritable, and the reason cta.py's own comment named OPS-PLANS-PUBLIC-PREPAY-FIELD-W1 as the wave that owed this field. That obligation is DISCHARGED here. The bot's Telegram plan picker now renders four SKUs (starter/pro x month/6month) with every figure derived from this endpoint. UNITS ARE UNCHANGED: monthly_calls and daily_calls are CALLS on the API's meter (one returned verdict, HOLD included); the Telegram bot's meter counts DELIVERED ALERTS and a silent HOLD stays free there — same NUMBER, different UNIT, per Rule 1 and Rule 3 of docs/METERING-DIVERGENCE.md.

forbidden_keys_note: UNCHANGED from 2026-08-27, and the camelCase priceUsd6Month entry deliberately SURVIVES the addition of the snake_case price_usd_6month. They are different strings: the public key is snake_case and the internal SoT field is camelCase, so the forbidden-substring test in tests/plans-public-api.test.ts still passes over a body that now carries the value. Keeping the entry is what stops a future wave from serialising the plans.ts record wholesale and shipping the internal field name alongside the public one.

_algovault.brand: The Brain Layer for AI Trading Agents
_algovault.note: Building an agent? Get a free API key — higher limits, all tools, x402 pay-per-call.

price_usd_6month_note: 🛑 TWO PROPERTIES, both load-bearing. (1) null is a REFUSAL — 'not sold on this term' — exactly as daily_calls' null is. It is never 0 and never a scaled monthly: plans.ts::planPrepayTotalUsd already refuses to fabricate a term nobody priced, and this field is that refusal projected onto the wire. A consumer coercing enterprise's null to 0 would advertise a free plan. (2) It is a TOTAL, not a monthly rate: 39.9 is what the card is charged once, for six months. A consumer rendering it beside price_usd MUST say which ('$39.90/6mo'), or the pair reads as a price cut. The endpoint projects it through planPrepayTotalUsd rather than reading plan.priceUsd6Month directly, so the 'never fabricate an unpriced term' decision has exactly ONE derivation. Both properties are pinned in tests/plans-public-api.test.ts and both were proven able to fail — see proven_able_to_fail.
null_daily_calls_note: enterprise.daily_calls is null, and null is a REFUSAL — not 'unlimited' and not zero. src/lib/plans.ts::planDailyCallsLabel carries the same warning for the copy path: no real Enterprise deal has set a daily cap, so a consumer must render the ABSENCE rather than substitute a number or the word 'unlimited', which PRICING-FLAT-CALL-BILLING-AND-6MONTH-W1 R-E removed from this ladder. A consumer that coerces null to 0 would refuse every Enterprise call; one that reads it as unlimited would publish a claim no contract supports. Pinned by tests/plans-public-api.test.ts.
generated_at_note: 🛑 generated_at is a RENDER STAMP, not a producer-freshness signal, and it is the ONLY per-request-varying field in the body. verification-gates.md — 'freshness alarms measure PRODUCERS, never rendered artifacts' — so no canary may key staleness on it: it reports the serving process's clock, not the ladder's cadence. The ladder changes only on deploy, and the container restart is its real invalidation boundary. It is emitted so a machine consumer can tell when a cached copy was minted, and it is documented here so a future freshness check does not mistake it for a producer stamp.
algovault_block_note: _algovault IS on the ALLOW-list, ratified by Mr.1 2026-08-27 (Q3=b). src/lib/public-cta.ts declares that any public JSON endpoint merges buildPublicCtaBlock(), and audits/public-cta-shape-snapshot-2026-07-15.json lists _algovault plus these four sub-keys under each adopting endpoint's allowed_keys. The block is an exported pure formatter returning static approved copy — no I/O, no live figures — so it changes neither the cost profile nor the cacheability of a static projection. Unchanged by this wave.
error_contract: No error path exists. buildPublicPlansBody() is total: it reads module-level constants and a frozen record, calls one pure total helper (planPrepayTotalUsd, which returns null rather than throwing on an unpriced term), performs no I/O, and cannot throw on any input — the route takes no parameters. There is no 4xx and no 5xx branch. An unreachable endpoint is an infrastructure fault, not an application state, and must be diagnosed as one.
auth_contract: UNAUTHENTICATED by design, unlike its register-site neighbours /api/bot/validate-key, /api/entitlement/* and /api/ops/build. The consumer this exists for is a FREE, unlinked Telegram chat, which holds no api_key and no internal key. Every field served is already public copy on algovault.com/#pricing and on the /signup plan cards. Adding auth here would recreate the exact gap the endpoint closes.

cache_contract.description: Cache-Control: public, max-age=300. No in-process cache: the handler is a pure projection with no DB touch, so caching it in-process would add an invalidation problem to a function that has none. The 300s TTL matches the bot's EXISTING five-minute entitlement-drain cadence (the ladder mirror rides that cron — no new schedule), so the mirror can never be more than one drain cycle behind an edge copy. UNCHANGED by this wave: an additive field does not move the invalidation boundary.
cache_contract.staleness_signal: NONE, deliberately. The ladder changes only on deploy and the container restart is the invalidation boundary. Do not key a freshness alarm on generated_at — see generated_at_note.

consumers: algovault-bot free-tier ladder mirror — src/algovault_bot/ladder_client.py::parse_ladder, fetched by the EXISTING entitlement_drain cron every 5 minutes and written to the free_tier_ladder SQLite table. LIVE since GROWTH-TG-QUOTA-PARITY-W1 CH2. WIDENED IN THE SAME WAVE AS THIS FIELD (GROWTH-TG-PLAN-PICKER-W1 R2) to mirror the full four-SKU ladder: starter/pro x month/6month plus both daily caps. Unknown-key tolerance is pinned there by a fixture carrying two invented extra keys, so the deploy ORDER of the two repos is free — an older bot ignores this field, and a newer bot reads it as absent (None) and serves its pinned fallback rather than refusing.

ops/pricing-tokens.json via scripts/emit-pricing-tokens.mjs — NOT a consumer of this endpoint, but a SECOND PROJECTION of the same source (dist/lib/plans.js). tests/plans-public-api.test.ts asserts the two agree on the free and paid CALL ladders. It does NOT yet carry a prepay token, and that is a deliberate non-change: no copy surface consumes one. 🛑 On a mismatch the fix is to REGENERATE the tokens from plans.ts — never to hand-edit either artifact to match the other, which would convert two projections into two SoTs.
proven_able_to_fail: tests/plans-public-api.test.ts, 17 tests (16 before this wave, +1 for the six-month term). Two deliberate breaks were run against the new assertions on 2026-09-06 and both went RED, then were restored to 17/17 green. (1) Coercing the refusal to a number — `planPrepayTotalUsd(...) ?? 0` — failed 2 of 17: the SoT-parity assertion and the enterprise-REFUSES assertion. (2) Reading the raw SoT field instead of the helper — `plan.priceUsd6Month` — failed 3 of 17, because enterprise's `undefined` is DELETED by JSON.stringify and the tier loses a key: the six-key ALLOW-list test caught it in addition to the other two. Break (2) is the one that matters, and it is why the field is projected through the helper: `undefined` and `null` look identical in TypeScript at this call site and differ completely on the wire.
drift_check_command: curl -fsS https://api.algovault.com/api/plans/public | jq -e '(keys == ["_algovault","free","generated_at","tiers"]) and (.free | keys == ["daily_calls","monthly_calls"]) and ([.tiers[] | keys] | flatten | unique == ["daily_calls","id","label","monthly_calls","price_usd","price_usd_6month"]) and ((.tiers | map(.id)) == ["starter","pro","enterprise"]) and ((.tiers[] | select(.id=="enterprise") | .daily_calls) == null) and ((.tiers[] | select(.id=="enterprise") | .price_usd_6month) == null) and (._algovault | keys == ["brand","docs","get_started","note"])' >/dev/null && ! curl -fsS https://api.algovault.com/api/plans/public | grep -qE 'outcome_(return_pct|price|won)|priceUsd(Annual|6Month|Monthly)|monthlyCalls|dailyCalls|customer_?[Cc]ount|api_?[Kk]ey' && echo PLANS_PUBLIC_SHAPE_OK
drift_check_note: The command asserts the ladder's SHAPE and its ordering, and separately greps for internal field names. It deliberately does NOT pin the VALUES 200/100/10000/39.9/129/etc: those are the ladder, and the ladder is allowed to change — pinning them here would make a legitimate price change look like a drift incident. What must never change without a wave is the key set, the tier order, enterprise's TWO nulls, and the absence of every forbidden key. Note that `[.tiers[] | keys] | flatten | unique` is a UNION across tiers, so it would not catch a single tier missing a key on its own; the per-tier equality that does catch that lives in tests/plans-public-api.test.ts, which is the right home for it because it runs on every push rather than on a cron. Value correctness lives in that same test (against plans.ts) and in scripts/emit-pricing-tokens.mjs --check (against dist/lib/plans.js) — two projections, one source.
superseded_reason: OPS-PLANS-PUBLIC-ENTERPRISE-DEPRICE-W1 CH1 nulled tiers[id=enterprise].price_usd and .monthly_calls, so this file no longer describes the live shape — its captured_body records price_usd: 299, which brand-facts.md:552 lists as a HIGH-severity forbidden phrase. ONE SNAPSHOT PER ENDPOINT: scripts/build-knowledge-json.mjs projects every audits/*-shape-snapshot-*.json into the knowledge bundle keyed by `response_shape:${endpoint}`, and both files carry the SAME endpoint string, so leaving this one live would publish two contradictory descriptions of one doc id — winkBM25 refuses the duplicate outright. This field is the ratified way to retire a shape (Q1, 2026-08-21): the builder and tests/unit/shape-snapshot-drift-checks.test.ts both SKIP a snapshot carrying it. NOTHING ELSE IN THIS FILE IS TOUCHED — every measurement, captured_body, date and note is byte-identical, because a dated ledger states what was true when written. This is a forward pointer, not a correction. The tempting alternative — rewording this file's `endpoint` so both coexist — is rejected for the reason that test's own comment gives: it would silently split one contract's history into two lineages, and would leave search_knowledge answering with the retired price.
